{{short description|Relation between the side lengths and angles of a spherical triangle}}
[[Image:Law-of-haversines.svg|right|thumb|Spherical triangle]]

In [[spherical trigonometry]], the '''half-side formula''' relates the angles and lengths of the sides of [[spherical triangle]]s, which are triangles drawn on the [[Spherical geometry|surface of a sphere]] and so have curved sides and do not obey the formulas for [[Triangle|plane triangle]]s.<ref>{{citation|title=Handbook of Mathematics|title-link=Bronshtein and Semendyayev|first1=I. N.|last1=Bronshtein|first2=K. A.|last2=Semendyayev|first3=Gerhard|last3=Musiol|first4=Heiner|last4=Mühlig|publisher=Springer|year=2007|isbn=9783540721222|page=165}}[https://books.google.com/books?id=gCgOoMpluh8C&pg=PA165]</ref>

For a triangle <math>\triangle ABC</math> on a sphere, the half-side formula is<ref>{{citation|title=The Penguin Dictionary of Mathematics|edition=4th|first=David|last=Nelson|publisher=Penguin UK|year=2008|isbn=9780141920870|page=529|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ud3sEeVdTIwC&pg=PT529}}.</ref>
<math display="block">\begin{align}
\tan \tfrac12 a
&= \sqrt{\frac{-\cos(S)\, \cos(S - A)}
              {\cos(S - B)\, \cos(S - C)} }
\end{align}</math>
where {{mvar|a}}, {{mvar|b}}, {{mvar|c}} are the angular lengths (measure of [[central angle]], arc lengths normalized to a [[unit sphere|sphere of unit radius]]) of the sides opposite angles {{mvar|A}}, {{mvar|B}}, {{mvar|C}} respectively, and <math>S = \tfrac12 (A+B+ C)</math> is half the sum of the angles. Two more formulas can be obtained for <math>b</math> and <math>c</math> by permuting the labels <math>A, B, C.</math>

The polar dual relationship for a spherical triangle is the ''half-angle formula'', 
<math display="block">\begin{align}
\tan \tfrac12 A
&= \sqrt{\frac{\sin(s - b)\, \sin(s - c)}
              {\sin(s)\, \sin(s - a)} }
\end{align}</math>
where semiperimeter <math>s = \tfrac12 (a + b + c)</math> is half the sum of the sides. Again, two more formulas can be obtained by permuting the labels <math>A, B, C.</math>

== Half-tangent variant ==

The same relationships can be written as rational equations of half-tangents (tangents of half-angles). If <math>t_a = \tan \tfrac12 a,</math> <math>t_b = \tan \tfrac12 b,</math> <math>t_c = \tan \tfrac12 c,</math> <math>t_A = \tan \tfrac12 A,</math> <math>t_B = \tan \tfrac12 B,</math> and <math>t_C = \tan \tfrac12 C,</math> then the half-side formula is equivalent to:
<math display="block">\begin{align}
t_a^2
&= \frac{\bigl(t_Bt_C + t_Ct_A + t_At_B - 1\bigr)\bigl({-t_Bt_C + t_Ct_A + t_At_B + 1}\bigr)}
        {\bigl(t_Bt_C - t_Ct_A + t_At_B + 1\bigr)\bigl(t_Bt_C + t_Ct_A - t_At_B + 1\bigr)},
\end{align}</math>
and the half-angle formula is equivalent to:
<math display="block">\begin{align}
t_A^2
&= \frac{\bigl(t_a - t_b + t_c + t_at_bt_c\bigr)\bigl(t_a + t_b - t_c + t_at_bt_c\bigr)}
        {\bigl(t_a + t_b + t_c - t_at_bt_c\bigr)\bigl({-t_a + t_b + t_c + t_at_bt_c}\bigr)}.
\end{align}</math>
